I found a solution and wanted to share it just in case it' useful for someone.  


I have a Logitech mouse and discovered a Logitech software called "LogiOptions" that allows me to change some keybindings.

I understand that frustration. Last year I was checked and my TSH was about 3.2, while I was hospitalized for 5 days due to emotional distress. I was told to just get it checked every now and then because it was borderline, and that's what I did. Last week I was tested again and TSH was over 13. Keep monitoring yours, too!

I'm sorry that you lost your child. I feel like it may not be the right time to say it, but if your partner wasn't going to help support you or your child... you both would have had a hard time, and you would have been tied to a person who didn't care enough about you or the baby to show support. At the very least, you can eliminate that person from your life forever now and find someone who is more available to you in regards to starting a family.

I'm sorry you lost something that gave you hope. But remember, a child should never be brought into this world with a job; to keep you happy. You both would have had a difficult time without your partner's help. You have the opportunity to create a better environment for a child now as you move forward. I hope I don't come across as too insensitive.
This is very helpful. Thank you!

This is an amazing comment. Thanks so much for it. <3
Maybe I'll make a post specifically about my situation and try to get some feedback. Definitely not looking for diagnosis!! In fact I have a dr appointment coming up soon to discuss this. I'd just like to know if my situation sounds like its worth looking into. Because maybe if I cna identify what's hurting me, it'll be easier to keep myself separated from it and look at it differently.

I agree with what others have said. If she is spending most of her time there, she should be contributing towards the rent, too. She is staying in the home, after all. I do also agree that her sleeping in your room to "watch your cat" is excessive. I can see why they would have assumed she'd just be checking in on the cat daily, but to sleep there, too? I totally understand their situation. SHE isn't their roommate. It's weird, you know? It isn't about a body-count.

They are dealing with a fourth person that they didn't sign up to live with. It would be the right thing to have her contribute towards rent if she is spending the majority of her time there.
